channel.title: Internal Prerequisite Analysis :: CS Two Year Refactor
channel.description:
Working draft for faculty review. This analysis looks inside the two-year core — not the upper-division chains — at what the course sequence’s interconnection means when reality intrudes: a student fails a course, drops mid-term, or enters off-sequence. CIS/MATH/STAT numbers are actual K-State courses (or, for the MATH/STAT modules, confirmed course slots in resources/reference/degree-maps/cs.md). flowchart TB %% Internal prerequisites of the two-year core (arrow = 'is required by'). In practice, that risk is narrow: CIS 116 and CIS 200, both taken in the first year, are the only courses whose failure has any real multi-course cascade risk — everything else in the two-year core either blocks nothing, or blocks at most one downstream course.
